added_claim_errors: Lists unopened self-service provinces as Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Shanghai, Tianjin, Heilongjiang, Qinghai, Xinjiang. The Liwan page I opened lists the same set without Tianjin, so Tianjin comes from another district page and is unverified here; Henan's absence is correct.
Says paper temporary rail proof at the station is free. The key notes there is no official basis for this.
Says self-service machines need only the 粤居码, no appointment, and some sites are open 24 hours. Unverified.
Says the 12306 page needs face re-verification after 30 minutes. Unverified.
Says the old card must be handed in when the new one is issued. Plausible but unsourced.
Gives no statutory 60-day limit, only the Guangzhou 40 days. The 40 days is confirmed on the Liwan page I opened, counted from submitting the cross-region registration form.
The Liwan link is mistyped (jczgkk instead of jczwgk) and returns 404 when opened, so the main cited source is not checkable as given.

Says a temporary ID at the hometown office is usually ready 当场或3日内. The three-day limit has a legal basis (Ministry of Public Security order No. 78), but the trap list flags same-day temporary IDs and the claim is unsourced in the answer.
Materials list names 户口簿, 居住证, 驾驶证, 护照 and 社保卡, plus contracts and lease. The Liwan page says only the photo receipt is required, so this overstates what is needed.
Says first-time ID applications can now be done across provinces. Unverified; 2017 sources say first applications still required returning to the hukou place.
Says the temporary ID takes about 1-2 weeks in Guangzhou. This is an estimate and is not sourced.
Says the paper temporary rail proof is free and valid for that day's travel. Free is flagged by the key as having no official basis, and day-only validity is unverified.
Says to bring 户口簿, 驾驶证 and 社保卡 to the station for checking. No basis; the answer itself marks them non-essential.
Cites a Panyu page for Guangzhou supporting remote loss reporting from 2016. Not opened; unverified.

reasons: Both answers correct the two false premises at the start, give 40 yuan and 10 yuan, give 12306 e-proof details (24 hours, 6 per month), and say the temporary ID will likely not arrive by 10/31. A is cleaner on the traps: it says no hukou booklet or residence permit is needed (matching the Liwan page), and it says outright that the temporary ID may not be ready by 10/31. B tells the user to bring several ID documents plus contracts, quotes a same-day-or-3-days temporary ID for the hometown, and has a broken (404) Liwan link. B is better on key point 4, where it states the statutory 60-day limit and A gives only the Guangzhou 40 days. Both are long, and B repeats the hometown route in the opening summary and again in section four. A wins slightly on trap handling and honesty.
